I had an interesting conversation with a man from another culture the other day and it brought something to the forefront of my mind.

Closeness is different from culture to culture and some cultures seem to lack it entirely or at least seem to push in the opposite direction.

My mind has been very clear lately and I've had the opportunity to drop my walls and any guards I had built up.

Strangely this has had an almost immediate affect on all relationships I have and I've quickly grown new ones.

The amount of closeness and knowledge you can gain from a person in just a few hours is an amazing thing. I was out with friends and met a stranger who had just had some relationship issues. We ended up connecting and talking for hours and hours and even sharing a back massage at one point. She said it was the closest she had felt to someone in years.

I love spreading this awareness that if we simply let ourselves be ourselves it opens up so many doors.

I'm a very closed off person, and hadn't realized it until I started working on self-development in recent months.

What it comes down to is I seem to have an automatically negative valuation of most people I come across, whether online or in real life – I expect the worse of them before I expect the best of them, and this is mainly as a result of life experience, but I'm working on getting better at that. When you combine that with a bad habit of historically suppressing emotions and striking out on my own in an effort to survive and be a functional human being, it's a detrimental combo that leads to massive difficulties in becoming close with people...

OP, If you have any advice for dropping those walls or seeing the good in people, let me know cause I'm still figuring it out myself. I don't want to be a robot anymore :/

The easiest ground to stand on is your own. I know it sounds philosophical but be comfortable in your own place and in your own thoughts and just let conversations happen. Really listen to the other person, share your perspectives and don't be afraid to share your own passions.

I'll be honest I was pretty guarded myself and it seems I put myself in that place. What helped clear my head was physical activity and a trip out into the wilderness. Something about being physical and out in nature makes you focus on yourself and the world around you. Cities and people can be very distracting and you can find yourself wondering and caring too much about things that have no influence over you.

We can chat more but I figured I'd respond with at least a blurb that I felt made sense.

In the past I would opt for silence in an effort to avoid confrontation, but I've been practicing voicing my thoughts and perspectives in the moment instead of holding back. It landed me in an argument with a co-worker this week, but I left that conversation feeling satisfied with my own contributions and glad that I didn't cave in or give up on talking in that situation.

As for physical activity, absolutely, I use it to clear my head and to work through things I didn't even know I needed to work through. I like to think of it as my version of meditation.
